sentinel_issue: The observed room count reached 46,522 on 2026-09-24, about 9.1× the documented 5,120-room cap. This indicates the room-count guard is not active or the telemetry is reading a different deployment, undermining the stated namespace and disk-bound guarantee.
worker_response: The data points to an aggregation/configuration mismatch, not simply a failed guard: rooms_capacity steps from 20,480 (4×5,120) to 40,960, 81,920, and 163,840 (32×5,120), while rooms_total peaks at 50,657 and is 46,522 on September 24. Tag metrics by deployment/namespace and report per-namespace counts; if 5,120 is intended as a global cap, enforce it in the shared allocator and add an alert when rooms_total exceeds it.
auditor_verdict: AGREE. The stepped capacities (20,480, 40,960, 81,920, then 163,840) and the 50,657 peak support a configuration/aggregation mismatch rather than proving a failed 5,120-room guard, though the data still shows the documented cap is not enforced in the measured aggregate: 46,522 is 9.1× 5,120.
